gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ the flames with buckets for an hour by the time the firemen arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour by the time … arrived' — past perfect continuous for duration before a past moment.

gaps.sentence: I ___ it matters whether we leave at six or seven — the traffic will be terrible either way.
gaps.hint: think meaning believe is a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Think' in the sense of 'believe' is a state verb, so the negative present simple is used: don't think.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ at six tomorrow morning, as it does every day.
gaps.explanation: Timetabled events use the present simple.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ to traffic every year for repainting in May.
gaps.explanation: A recurring scheduled event takes the present simple.
